notes:
Version 0.2.3.

The spacing inside a line of the public screen can be set in the look of the draw: the room given to the place number, the space between the team name and its statistics, the space between two statistics and the width of one. The defaults keep the previous layout; tightening them leaves more room to the names.

Version 0.2.2.

On the public screen, a long team name no longer pushes the list off screen. The two columns keep strictly the same width, and a name too long for its slot is condensed: the letters first move closer together, then the characters are narrowed. The summary does the same.

Version 0.2.1.

The summary on the public screen lists the team lists only: the season's stages are announced, not drawn, and are no category of the result.

On the commentators' screen, a "back to live" button appears as soon as the commentator picks another team or another category, and returns to the last place given.

Version 0.2.0.

A new kind of list for the season's stages: nothing is drawn, each stage is shown on its own card, in its own order, as the speaker announces it. A save of the former page that entered the stages as teams is recognised and converted, venue and dates split apart.

The control page gives the club codes of each list in drawn order, ready to paste into the Setup screen of the new season's first division competition; the list is refused while a team has no club code, since that screen would shift every following team.

On the commentators' screen, a figure that is the best, second or third of its category is shown in gold, silver or bronze.

The settings of a draw are easier to find again: the draw's title opens them from the list, and the page says that every change is saved as it is made.

Version 0.1.0.

First version. Screens for a live draw ceremony, independent of any competition: a public screen with an animated background that reveals each team as it is drawn, a control page to record the draw, and a commentators' screen.

The commentators see each team's history and notes, and — when the draw is tied to the previous season's ianseo competition — its final rank, matches won and lost, points per arrow, results and qualification stage by stage, and the archers who shot for it, with their national rankings when the REPARTITION_EPREUVES module has downloaded them. Rankings are read through the core's Rank classes.

The screens synchronise through the server, so the public screen, the control page and the commentators' tablets can run on different machines. A save of the stand-alone HTML draw page used before can be imported.
